svg.title: Partner[v] from S — the staleness trap, animated
svg.desc: Animated SVG of Prim's S-side partner-array maintenance. S and V\S are drawn as labelled regions; as picks happen, vertices migrate from V\S into S and the boundary moves right. Whenever partner[a] ends up entirely inside S (both endpoints in S, no longer crossing the cut), it is stale. A rescan finds a's new lightest V\S-neighbour. Across 4 iterations, partner[a] goes stale 4 times in a row — 3 + 2 + 1 + 0 = 6 wasted edge scans charged to a single vertex. The bottom pills accumulate that running cost.
svg.text: S-side bookkeeping — partner[v] for v ∈ S = lightest V \ S-neighbour

g.text: Step 0 · init. S = {a}. Scan a's V\S-neighbours {b, c, d, e} → partner[a] = (a, b).
Step 1 · pick (a–b), w=1. b crossed into S — partner[a] = (a, b) now sits ENTIRELY inside S → stale. Rescan: 3 edges.
Step 2 · pick (a–c), w=2. c crossed into S — partner[a] = (a, c) now sits ENTIRELY inside S → stale. Rescan: 2 edges.
Step 3 · pick (a–d), w=3. d crossed into S — partner[a] = (a, d) now sits ENTIRELY inside S → stale. Rescan: 1 edge.
Step 4 · pick (a–e), w=4. e crossed into S — partner[a] = (a, e) now sits ENTIRELY inside S → stale. Rescan: 0 edges (no V\S-neighbours left).
